<h1 id="kintone-rest-api">Kintone REST API v2026.8.31</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

OpenAPI specification for Kintone's REST API.

## Authentication
Each operation can be executed with either **API token authentication (recommended)** or **password authentication** (see `security`). Because API tokens are scoped per app, some APIs—such as user/organization/group management (User API) and space administration—cannot be run with a token and require **password authentication**.

If **Basic authentication (access restriction)** or **secure access (client certificate)** is enabled on your environment, you must additionally provide an extra gate (`Authorization: Basic ...` header / client certificate) on top of the above. **Session authentication** (browser cookie + CSRF token) is available on virtually all APIs, but this spec targets server-to-server integration and therefore does not include it in `security`. Details of these methods that `security` cannot express are described in a structured form under `x-kintone-additional-auth` at the document root.

## Limitations (Kintone-specific)
- **Record schemas are dynamic per app.** Field codes are arbitrary keys (`additionalProperties`) and values are represented as a union per field type (`oneOf`/`anyOf` with a `type` discriminator). The exact types of an individual app cannot be fully expressed, so supplement real app types with examples / fixtures.
- **When a GET query is long**, you can avoid URL-length limits by sending `POST` with the `X-HTTP-Method-Override: GET` header and putting parameters in the body (the server processes it as GET). Such GET operations are marked with `x-kintone-method-override: true`. No duplicate operation is defined; the GET definition is authoritative.
- **Authentication differs per endpoint.** Which methods (API token / password / OAuth2) each API accepts is taken directly from the "Authentication" row of the official documentation pages (cybozu.dev) via harvest and reflected in `security`. Management APIs that do not support tokens (space/guest administration, app move, plugins, statistics, etc.) end up as password authentication only. Only the OAuth2 scope each operation needs is a best-effort estimate derived from the path family, because no machine-readable scope mapping is published.

# Authentication

* API Key (apiToken)
    - Parameter Name: **X-Cybozu-API-Token**, in: header. API token authentication (recommended). Specify a token generated in the app settings in the X-Cybozu-API-Token header. To target multiple apps, list tokens separated by commas. Because tokens are scoped per app, some APIs such as user/organization/group management (User API) and space administration require password authentication.

* API Key (passwordAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **X-Cybozu-Authorization**, in: header. Password authentication. Specify the Base64-encoded value of `login-name:password` in the X-Cybozu-Authorization header. Use it for APIs that cannot be executed with an API token (User API, space administration, etc.). Intended for server-side use; do not enter credentials into a shared or public Try console.

- oAuth2 authentication. OAuth2 authentication (authorization code flow). Used when a user delegates permissions to a third-party app. Requires prior OAuth client registration (client ID/secret); the required scopes are specified per operation in `security`. Use exactly one method; it is not combined with token/password authentication.

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [https://{subdomain}.cybozu.com/oauth2/authorization](https://{subdomain}.cybozu.com/oauth2/authorization)
    - Token URL = [https://{subdomain}.cybozu.com/oauth2/token](https://{subdomain}.cybozu.com/oauth2/token)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|k:app_record:read|Read records.|
|k:app_record:write|Add, update, and delete records.|
|k:app_settings:read|Read app settings.|
|k:app_settings:write|Change app settings.|
|k:file:read|Download files.|
|k:file:write|Upload files.|

## Get app (guest space)

<a id="opIdgetAppForGuestSpace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.cybozu.com/k/guest/0/v1/app.json?id=0' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cybozu-API-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /k/guest/{guestSpaceId}/v1/app.json`

Gets general information of an App, including the name, description, related Space, creator and updater information.

<h3 id="get-app-guest-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|guestSpaceId|path|integer(int64)|true|Guest space ID (the number that appears in the space URL /k/#/space/<ID> when the space is open in a browser).|
|id|query|integer(int64)|true|The App ID.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "threadId": "string",
  "spaceId": "string",
  "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "creator": {
    "code": "string",
    "name": "string"
  },
  "code": "string",
  "modifiedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "appId": "string",
  "modifier": {
    "code": "string",
    "name": "string"
  },
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string"
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

<h3 id="get-app-guest-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of app/get|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

<h3 id="get-app-guest-space-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|threadId|string \| null|true|none|none|
|spaceId|string \| null|true|none|none|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|creator|object|true|none|none|
|» code|string|false|none|none|
|» name|string|false|none|none|
|code|string|true|none|none|
|modifiedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|appId|string|true|none|none|
|modifier|object|true|none|none|
|» code|string|false|none|none|
|» name|string|false|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|description|string|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiToken, passwordAuth, oauth2 ( Scopes: k:app_settings:read )
</aside>

## Put app acl (guest space)

<a id="opIdputAppAclForGuestSpace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.cybozu.com/k/guest/0/v1/app/acl.json \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cybozu-API-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "app": 0,
    "rights": [
      {
        "recordImportable": true,
        "appEditable": true,
        "recordExportable": true,
        "recordAddable": true,
        "recordViewable": true,
        "recordEditable": true,
        "recordDeletable": true,
        "includeSubs": true,
        "entity": {
          "code": "string",
          "type": "USER"
        }
      }
    ],
    "revision": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /k/guest/{guestSpaceId}/v1/app/acl.json`

Updates the App permissions of an App.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "app": 0,
  "rights": [
    {
      "recordImportable": true,
      "appEditable": true,
      "recordExportable": true,
      "recordAddable": true,
      "recordViewable": true,
      "recordEditable": true,
      "recordDeletable": true,
      "includeSubs": true,
      "entity": {
        "code": "string",
        "type": "USER"
      }
    }
  ],
  "revision": 0
}
```

<h3 id="put-app-acl-guest-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|guestSpaceId|path|integer(int64)|true|Guest space ID (the number that appears in the space URL /k/#/space/<ID> when the space is open in a browser).|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» app|body|integer(int64)|true|The App ID.|
|» rights|body|[[AppAclPutRight](#schemaappaclputright)]|true|An array listing data of App permissions, in order of priority.<br>The "Everyone" group will be treated with the lowest priority, wherever it is placed in the list.|
|» revision|body|integer(int64)|false|Specify the revision number of the settings that will be deployed.<br>The request will fail if the revision number is not the latest revision.<br>The revision will not be checked if this parameter is ignored, or -1 is specified.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "revision": "string"
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

<h3 id="put-app-acl-guest-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of app/acl/put|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

<h3 id="put-app-acl-guest-space-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|revision|string|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiToken, passwordAuth, oauth2 ( Scopes: k:app_settings:write )
</aside>

## Get apps (guest space)

<a id="opIdgetAppsForGuestSpace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.cybozu.com/k/guest/0/v1/apps.json \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cybozu-Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /k/guest/{guestSpaceId}/v1/apps.json`

Gets general information of multiple Apps, including the name, description, related Space, creator and updater information.

<h3 id="get-apps-guest-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|guestSpaceId|path|integer(int64)|true|Guest space ID (the number that appears in the space URL /k/#/space/<ID> when the space is open in a browser).|
|codes|query|[string]|false|The App Code.<br>Up to 100 App Codes can be specified.<br>Each App Code must be between 1 to 64 characters. An exact match search will be used, and will be case sensitive.<br>If `null` or an empty array is specified, this parameter will be ignored.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of retrievals that will be skipped.<br>Must be between 0 and 2,147,483,647. If nothing is specified, it will default to 0.|
|name|query|string|false|The App Name or a part of it.<br>Each App Name must be specified within 64 characters.<br>A partial search will be used, and the search will be case insensitive.<br>The localized name of the App in the user's locale will also be included in the search.<br>If `null` or an empty array is specified, this parameter will be ignored.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of Apps to retrieve.<br>Must be between 1 and 100.<br>If nothing is specified, it will default to 100.|
|ids|query|[string(long)]|false|The App IDs.<br>Integers from 1 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 can be specified.<br>Up to 100 IDs can be specified.<br>If `null` or an empty array is specified, this parameter will be ignored.|
|spaceIds|query|[string(long)]|false|The Space ID of where the App resides in.<br>Integers from 1 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 can be specified.<br>Up to 100 IDs can be specified.<br>If `null` or an empty array is specified, this parameter will be ignored.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "apps": [
    {
      "threadId": "string",
      "spaceId": "string",
      "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "creator": {
        "code": "string",
        "name": "string"
      },
      "code": "string",
      "modifiedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "appId": "string",
      "modifier": {
        "code": "string",
        "name": "string"
      },
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

<h3 id="get-apps-guest-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of apps/get|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

## Get apps

<a id="opIdgetApps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.cybozu.com/k/v1/apps.json \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cybozu-Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /k/v1/apps.json`

Gets general information of multiple Apps, including the name, description, related Space, creator and updater information.

<h3 id="get-apps-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|codes|query|[string]|false|The App Code.<br>Up to 100 App Codes can be specified.<br>Each App Code must be between 1 to 64 characters. An exact match search will be used, and will be case sensitive.<br>If `null` or an empty array is specified, this parameter will be ignored.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of retrievals that will be skipped.<br>Must be between 0 and 2,147,483,647. If nothing is specified, it will default to 0.|
|name|query|string|false|The App Name or a part of it.<br>Each App Name must be specified within 64 characters.<br>A partial search will be used, and the search will be case insensitive.<br>The localized name of the App in the user's locale will also be included in the search.<br>If `null` or an empty array is specified, this parameter will be ignored.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of Apps to retrieve.<br>Must be between 1 and 100.<br>If nothing is specified, it will default to 100.|
|ids|query|[string(long)]|false|The App IDs.<br>Integers from 1 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 can be specified.<br>Up to 100 IDs can be specified.<br>If `null` or an empty array is specified, this parameter will be ignored.|
|spaceIds|query|[string(long)]|false|The Space ID of where the App resides in.<br>Integers from 1 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 can be specified.<br>Up to 100 IDs can be specified.<br>If `null` or an empty array is specified, this parameter will be ignored.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "apps": [
    {
      "threadId": "string",
      "spaceId": "string",
      "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "creator": {
        "code": "string",
        "name": "string"
      },
      "code": "string",
      "modifiedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "appId": "string",
      "modifier": {
        "code": "string",
        "name": "string"
      },
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

<h3 id="get-apps-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of apps/get|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

```bash
    "requests": [

            "property1": {
              "type": "CHECK_BOX",

              "type": "CHECK_BOX",
              "value": [

            }
          }
        },
        "api": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /k/guest/{guestSpaceId}/v1/bulkRequest.json`

```json
    {
      "method": "string",

        "app": 0,

          "property1": {

            "value": [

            ]
          },
          "property2": {

            ]
```

## Post preview app (guest space)

<a id="opIdpostPreviewAppForGuestSpace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.cybozu.com/k/guest/0/v1/preview/app.json \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cybozu-Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "thread": 0,
    "space": 0
  }'
```

`POST /k/guest/{guestSpaceId}/v1/preview/app.json`

Creates a preview App.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "thread": 0,
  "space": 0
}
```

<h3 id="post-preview-app-guest-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|guestSpaceId|path|integer(int64)|true|Guest space ID (the number that appears in the space URL /k/#/space/<ID> when the space is open in a browser).|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The App name.<br>The maximum length is 64 characters.|
|» thread|body|integer(int64)|false|The Thread ID of the thread in the Space where the App will be created.<br>*It is recommended to ignore this parameter so that Apps are created in the default thread. There is currently no helpful reason to create Apps in threads other than the default thread, as there are no visual representations in Kintone of Apps being related to threads. There are only visual representations of Apps being related to Spaces.|
|» space|body|integer(int64)|false|The Space ID of where the App will be created.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "app": "string",
  "revision": "string"
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

<h3 id="post-preview-app-guest-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of preview/app/post|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

<h3 id="post-preview-app-guest-space-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|app|string|false|none|none|
|revision|string|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
passwordAuth, oauth2 ( Scopes: k:app_settings:write )
</aside>

`PUT /k/v1/preview/app/settings.json`

Updates the description, name, icon, revision and color theme of an App.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "app": 0,
  "enableComments": "string",
  "titleField": {
    "code": "string",
    "selectionMode": "AUTO"
  },
  "icon": {
    "type": "FILE",
    "key": "APP1"
  },
  "description": "string",
  "enableThumbnails": "string",
  "enableDuplicateRecord": "string",
  "revision": 0,
  "enableInlineRecordEditing": "string",
  "enableBulkDeletion": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "theme": "WHITE",
  "numberPrecision": {
    "roundingMode": "HALF_EVEN",
    "decimalPlaces": 0,
    "digits": 0
  },
  "firstMonthOfFiscalYear": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="put-preview-app-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» app|body|integer(int64)|true|The App ID.|
|» enableComments|body|string|false|The **Enable comments** setting.|
|» titleField|body|object|false|The record title.|
|» » code|body|string|false|The field code of the field used as the title of the record. Required, if `MANUAL` is set for the `titleField.selectionMode` parameter.|
|» » selectionMode|body|string|true|The option of **The field to be used as the record title** settings.<br>- `AUTO`: The **Set automatically** option.<br>- `MANUAL`: The **Set manually** option.<br>Required if `titleField` is specified.|
|» icon|body|object|false|An object containing information of the App icon.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[PreviewAppSettingsPutIconPresetForm](#schemapreviewappsettingsputiconpresetform)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[PreviewAppSettingsPutIconFileForm](#schemapreviewappsettingsputiconfileform)|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|The App description. The maximum character limit is 10,000. HTML tags can be used.|
|» enableThumbnails|body|string|false|The **Show thumbnails** setting.|
|» enableDuplicateRecord|body|string|false|The **Enable the feature to "duplicate record"** setting.|
|» revision|body|integer(int64)|false|Specify the revision number of the settings that will be deployed.<br>The request will fail if the revision number is not the latest revision.<br>The revision will not be checked if this parameter is ignored, or `-1` is specified.|
|» enableInlineRecordEditing|body|string|false|The **Enable inline record editing** setting.|
|» enableBulkDeletion|body|string|false|The **Enable bulk deletion of records** setting.|
|» name|body|string|false|The App name. The maximum character limit is 64.|
|» theme|body|string|false|The Color theme.<br>The following can be specified:<br>- `WHITE`: Default<br>- `RED`<br>- `BLUE`<br>- `GREEN`<br>- `YELLOW`<br>- `BLACK`|
|» numberPrecision|body|object|false|The **Precision of numbers and calculations** setting.<br>For more information, refer to the following article on the Kintone Help site:<br>[Precision of numbers and calculations](https://us.kintone.help/k/en/id/040508#autocalc_rounding_30)|
|» » roundingMode|body|string|false|The **Rounding** setting<br>- `HALF_EVEN`: Round to nearest even number<br>- `UP`: Round up<br>- `DOWN`: Round down|
|» » decimalPlaces|body|number|false|The **Number of Decimal Places to Round** setting.<br>Specify an integer from 0 to 10.|
|» » digits|body|number|false|The **Total Number of Digits** setting.<br>Specify an integer from 1 to 30.|
|» firstMonthOfFiscalYear|body|string|false|The **First month of Fiscal Year** setting. Specify an integer from 1 to 12, representing the month.|

|» » selectionMode|MANUAL|

|» theme|CLIPBOARD|
|» theme|BINDER|

|» theme|CLIPS|
|» theme|RED|
|» theme|GREEN|
|» theme|BLUE|
|» theme|YELLOW|
|» theme|BLACK|
|» » roundingMode|HALF_EVEN|
|» » roundingMode|UP|
|» » roundingMode|DOWN|

## Put record (guest space)

<a id="opIdputRecordForGuestSpace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.cybozu.com/k/guest/0/v1/record.json \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cybozu-API-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "app": 0,
    "updateKey": {
      "field": "string",
      "value": "string"
    },
    "record": {
      "property1": {
        "type": "CHECK_BOX",
        "value": [
          "string"
        ]
      },
      "property2": {
        "type": "CHECK_BOX",
        "value": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    },
    "id": 0,
    "revision": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /k/guest/{guestSpaceId}/v1/record.json`

Updates details of 1 record in an App by specifying its record number, or a different unique key.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "app": 0,
  "updateKey": {
    "field": "string",
    "value": "string"
  },
  "record": {
    "property1": {
      "type": "CHECK_BOX",
      "value": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "property2": {
      "type": "CHECK_BOX",
      "value": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  },
  "id": 0,
  "revision": 0
}
```

<h3 id="put-record-guest-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|guestSpaceId|path|integer(int64)|true|Guest space ID (the number that appears in the space URL /k/#/space/<ID> when the space is open in a browser).|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» app|body|integer(int64)|true|The App ID.|
|» updateKey|body|object|false|The unique key of the record to be updated. Required, if _id_ will not be specified. To specify this field, the field must have the "Prohibit duplicate values" option turned on.|
|» » field|body|string|true|The field code of the unique key.<br>Required, if _updateKey_ will be specified.|
|» » value|body|string|true|The value of the unique key.<br>Required, if _updateKey_ will be specified.|
|» record|body|object|false|Field codes and values are specified in this object. If ignored, the record will not be updated. For more information on field types, refer to the following article:<br>[Field Types](https://kintone.dev/en/docs/kintone/overview/field-types/)|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[RecordWritableObject](#schemarecordwritableobject)|false|The value of a single field when writing a record.<br><br>**Always an object with a `value` property, never a bare value.**<br><br>```<br>correct: { "fieldCode": { "value": "ABC" } }<br>wrong:   { "fieldCode": "ABC" }<br>```<br><br>Sending a bare value returns HTTP 400. `type` is optional; when omitted, the App's field settings are used.<br><br>The shape of `value` depends on the field type, which `GET /k/v1/app/form/fields.json` reports:<br><br>\| Field type \| shape of `value` \|<br>\|---\|---\|<br>\| Single-line text, Multi-line text, Rich text, Link, Number, Date, Time, Date and time, Drop-down, Radio button \| string — numbers and dates are strings too, e.g. `"1200000"`, `"2026-08-31"` \|<br>\| Check box, Multi-choice \| array of strings, each matching one of the App's choices exactly \|<br>\| User selection, Department selection, Group selection \| array of `{ "code": "..." }` \|<br>\| Attachment \| array of `{ "fileKey": "..." }` — upload the file first to obtain a key \|<br>\| Table \| array of `{ "id": "...", "value": { "<fieldCode>": { "value": ... } } }` \|<br><br>To clear a field, send an empty string for the text-like types, or an empty array for the array types.<br><br>**A field code that does not exist in the App is silently ignored.** The request still returns HTTP 200 and a new revision, so a typo looks like success even though nothing changed. Copy the codes from `GET /k/v1/app/form/fields.json` exactly.<br><br>**Table and Attachment fields are replaced, not merged.** When updating an existing record, every table row and every `fileKey` the request does not list is deleted. To change one cell of a table, send the whole table including the `id` of each row to keep. Fields left out of the request entirely are untouched.|
|» id|body|integer(int64)|false|The Record ID of the record to be updated. Required, if _updateKey_ will not be specified.|
|» revision|body|integer(int64)|false|The expected revision number. If the value does not match, an error will occur and the record will not be updated. If the value is not specified or is -1, the revision number will not be checked.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "revision": "string"
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of record/put|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

`GET /k/guest/{guestSpaceId}/v1/records.json`

<h3 id="get-records-guest-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|query|query|string(query)|false|The search condition, written in Kintone's own query syntax. This is **not** SQL and **not** OData.<br>Ignoring this parameter returns all records that the credential can access.<br><br>The authoritative reference is [Query Strings](https://kintone.dev/en/docs/kintone/overview/query-string/). Its rules are reproduced below so that a correct query can be built without leaving this document.<br><br>## Syntax rules<br><br>- The field code always goes on the **left** of the operator, never on the right.<br>- Wrap string values in double quotes: `Status in ("Closed")`. Numbers and times are unquoted: `price > 10`, `Time > 10:00`.<br>- Combine conditions with `and` / `or`, and group them with parentheses.<br>- Field codes are defined per App and are case-sensitive. Call `GET /k/v1/app/form/fields.json` first to obtain the exact field codes and their types. Do not guess field codes.<br><br>## Operators allowed per field type<br><br>Using an operator that the field type does not support returns an error, so check the field type first.<br><br>\| Field type \| Allowed operators \|<br>\|---\|---\|<br>\| Single-line text, Link \| `=` `!=` `in` `not in` `like` `not like` \|<br>\| Multi-line text \| `like` `not like` `is empty` `is not empty` — **`=` is not allowed** \|<br>\| Rich text \| `like` `not like` \|<br>\| Number, Calculated \| `=` `!=` `>` `<` `>=` `<=` `in` `not in` \|<br>\| Drop-down, Radio button, Check box, Multi-choice \| **`in` / `not in` only — `=` is not allowed** \|<br>\| Date, Date and time, Time \| `=` `!=` `>` `<` `>=` `<=` \|<br>\| Created datetime, Updated datetime \| `=` `!=` `>` `<` `>=` `<=` \|<br>\| User selection, Department selection, Group selection \| `in` `not in` \|<br>\| Created by, Updated by \| `in` `not in` \|<br>\| Status \| `=` `!=` `in` `not in` \|<br>\| Record number, `$id` \| `=` `!=` `>` `<` `>=` `<=` `in` `not in` \|<br>\| Attachment \| `like` `not like` `is empty` `is not empty` \|<br>\| Lookup \| Same as the field type it looks up \|<br>\| Related Records, fields inside a Table \| Same as the source field type, but `=` and `!=` are **not** allowed — use `in` / `not in` \|<br>\| Field group, Category \| Cannot be used in a query \|<br><br>To reference a field inside a Related Records field, use `<relatedRecordsFieldCode>.<fieldCode>`.<br><br>## Functions<br><br>\| Function \| Applies to \|<br>\|---\|---\|<br>\| `LOGINUSER()` \| User selection, Created by, Updated by \|<br>\| `PRIMARY_ORGANIZATION()` \| Department selection \|<br>\| `NOW()` `TODAY()` `YESTERDAY()` `TOMORROW()` \| Date, Date and time, Created datetime, Updated datetime \|<br>\| `FROM_TODAY(n, "DAYS"\\|"WEEKS"\\|"MONTHS"\\|"YEARS")` \| same as above \|<br>\| `THIS_WEEK(SUNDAY..SATURDAY)` `LAST_WEEK()` `NEXT_WEEK()` \| same as above \|<br>\| `THIS_MONTH(1..31\\|LAST)` `LAST_MONTH()` `NEXT_MONTH()` \| same as above \|<br>\| `THIS_YEAR()` `LAST_YEAR()` `NEXT_YEAR()` \| same as above \|<br><br>Arguments may be omitted to mean the whole week / month / year, e.g. `THIS_MONTH()`. Time fields accept no functions.<br><br>## Options<br><br>Place these **after all conditions, in this exact order**: `order by`, `limit`, `offset`.<br><br>\| Option \| Meaning \|<br>\|---\|---\|<br>\| `order by <fieldCode> asc\\|desc` \| Sort order. Separate multiple fields with commas. Defaults to record ID descending. \|<br>\| `limit <n>` \| Number of records to return. Default 100, **maximum 500 for this API**. \|<br>\| `offset <n>` \| Number of records to skip. **Maximum 10000.** To read past 10000 records, use the cursor API (`POST /k/v1/records/cursor.json`) instead. \|<br><br>## Escaping<br><br>Inside double quotes, escape `"` and `\` with a backslash. This is required for single-line text, multi-line text, rich text, check box, radio button, drop-down, multi-choice and status fields.<br>Example: `Checkbox in ("sample\"1\"")`<br><br>## Examples<br><br>```<br>Text like "sample" and Text_area like "sample" order by Created_datetime desc<br>Drop_down in ("value1", "value2") and (Multi_choice in ("value3") or Radio_button in ("value4"))<br>Time > 10:00 and Time < 19:00 and Created_datetime = TODAY() order by $id asc limit 10<br>User_selection in (LOGINUSER()) and Department_selection not in (PRIMARY_ORGANIZATION())<br>Company_DB.company_name in ("kintone") and Company_DB.location like "San Francisco"<br>Text_area is empty<br>```|
|fields|query|[string]|false|The field codes to be included in the response.<br>Ignoring this parameter will return all accessible fields that exist in the App.<br>When specifying this parameter in the request body, the number of field codes that can be specified is up to 1,000.<br>When specifying this parameter in a query string, the maximum index is 99.<br>Fields in a table cannot be specified.<br>To retrieve a field in a table, specify the field code of the table field. All fields in the table will be retrieved.|
|totalCount|query|string(boolean)|false|If set to `true`, the total count of records that match the query conditions will be included in the response.<br>Ignoring this parameter will return `null`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "records": [
    {
      "property1": {
        "type": "CALC",
        "value": "777888999"
      },
      "property2": {
        "type": "CALC",
        "value": "777888999"
      }
    }
  ],
  "totalCount": "string"
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

|200|OK|success case of records/get|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

## Post records (guest space)

<a id="opIdpostRecordsForGuestSpace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.cybozu.com/k/guest/0/v1/records.json \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cybozu-API-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "app": 0,
    "records": [
      {
        "property1": {
          "type": "CHECK_BOX",
          "value": [
            "string"
          ]
        },
        "property2": {
          "type": "CHECK_BOX",
          "value": [
            "string"
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /k/guest/{guestSpaceId}/v1/records.json`

Adds multiple records to an App.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "app": 0,
  "records": [
    {
      "property1": {
        "type": "CHECK_BOX",
        "value": [
          "string"
        ]
      },
      "property2": {
        "type": "CHECK_BOX",
        "value": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="post-records-guest-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|guestSpaceId|path|integer(int64)|true|Guest space ID (the number that appears in the space URL /k/#/space/<ID> when the space is open in a browser).|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» app|body|integer(int64)|true|The App ID.|
|» records|body|[object]|true|Holds an array of record objects, that contains field codes and their values.<br>The values that can be specified vary depending on the type of field.<br>Fields that are not included in the objects are added with their default value.<br>Objects containing field codes that do not exist are ignored.<br>For more information on field types, refer to the following article:<br>[Field Types](https://kintone.dev/en/docs/kintone/overview/field-types/)|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[RecordWritableObject](#schemarecordwritableobject)|false|The value of a single field when writing a record.<br><br>**Always an object with a `value` property, never a bare value.**<br><br>```<br>correct: { "fieldCode": { "value": "ABC" } }<br>wrong:   { "fieldCode": "ABC" }<br>```<br><br>Sending a bare value returns HTTP 400. `type` is optional; when omitted, the App's field settings are used.<br><br>The shape of `value` depends on the field type, which `GET /k/v1/app/form/fields.json` reports:<br><br>\| Field type \| shape of `value` \|<br>\|---\|---\|<br>\| Single-line text, Multi-line text, Rich text, Link, Number, Date, Time, Date and time, Drop-down, Radio button \| string — numbers and dates are strings too, e.g. `"1200000"`, `"2026-08-31"` \|<br>\| Check box, Multi-choice \| array of strings, each matching one of the App's choices exactly \|<br>\| User selection, Department selection, Group selection \| array of `{ "code": "..." }` \|<br>\| Attachment \| array of `{ "fileKey": "..." }` — upload the file first to obtain a key \|<br>\| Table \| array of `{ "id": "...", "value": { "<fieldCode>": { "value": ... } } }` \|<br><br>To clear a field, send an empty string for the text-like types, or an empty array for the array types.<br><br>**A field code that does not exist in the App is silently ignored.** The request still returns HTTP 200 and a new revision, so a typo looks like success even though nothing changed. Copy the codes from `GET /k/v1/app/form/fields.json` exactly.<br><br>**Table and Attachment fields are replaced, not merged.** When updating an existing record, every table row and every `fileKey` the request does not list is deleted. To change one cell of a table, send the whole table including the `id` of each row to keep. Fields left out of the request entirely are untouched.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "revisions": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

<h3 id="post-records-guest-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of records/post|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|[string]|true|none|none|
|revisions|[string]|true|none|none|

apiToken, passwordAuth, oauth2 ( Scopes: k:app_record:write )

## Post records cursor (guest space)

<a id="opIdpostRecordsCursorForGuestSpace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.cybozu.com/k/guest/0/v1/records/cursor.json \

      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /k/guest/{guestSpaceId}/v1/records/cursor.json`

Adds a cursor so that large amount of records can be obtained from an App.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "app": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "query": "string",
  "fields": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="post-records-cursor-guest-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|guestSpaceId|path|integer(int64)|true|Guest space ID (the number that appears in the space URL /k/#/space/<ID> when the space is open in a browser).|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» app|body|integer(int64)|true|The App ID.|
|» size|body|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of records the Get Cursor API can retrieve from this cursor with one request.<br>The maximum number is 500 records. If ignored, the default number of records to be retrieved is 100.<br>To retrieve all records, repeatedly call the Get Cursor API.<br>For more information, refer to the following article:<br>[Get Cursor](https://kintone.dev/en/docs/kintone/rest-api/records/get-cursor/)|
|» query|body|string(query)|false|The search condition for the records the cursor will walk over, written in Kintone's own query syntax.<br>The operators and functions are the same as for the `query` parameter of `GET /k/v1/records.json` — see that parameter for the table of operators each field type allows.<br><br>**`order by`, `limit` and `offset` cannot be used here.** The cursor manages paging itself: set the batch size with the `size` parameter, then call `GET /k/v1/records/cursor.json` repeatedly until it reports `next: false`.<br><br>Ignoring this parameter creates a cursor over all records that the credential can access.|
|» fields|body|[string]|false|The field codes to be included in the response when using the Get Cursor API. For more information, refer to the following document:<br>[Get Cursor](https://kintone.dev/en/docs/kintone/rest-api/records/get-cursor/)<br>If ignored, all accessible fields in the app will be returned.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "totalCount": "string"
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

<h3 id="post-records-cursor-guest-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of records/cursor/post|Inline|

## Put record

<a id="opIdputRecord"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.cybozu.com/k/v1/record.json \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cybozu-API-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "app": 0,
    "updateKey": {
      "field": "string",
      "value": "string"
    },
    "record": {
      "property1": {
        "type": "CHECK_BOX",
        "value": [
          "string"
        ]
      },
      "property2": {
        "type": "CHECK_BOX",
        "value": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    },
    "id": 0,
    "revision": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /k/v1/record.json`

Updates details of 1 record in an App by specifying its record number, or a different unique key.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "app": 0,
  "updateKey": {
    "field": "string",
    "value": "string"
  },
  "record": {
    "property1": {
      "type": "CHECK_BOX",
      "value": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "property2": {
      "type": "CHECK_BOX",
      "value": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  },
  "id": 0,
  "revision": 0
}
```

<h3 id="put-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» app|body|integer(int64)|true|The App ID.|
|» updateKey|body|object|false|The unique key of the record to be updated. Required, if _id_ will not be specified. To specify this field, the field must have the "Prohibit duplicate values" option turned on.|
|» » field|body|string|true|The field code of the unique key.<br>Required, if _updateKey_ will be specified.|
|» » value|body|string|true|The value of the unique key.<br>Required, if _updateKey_ will be specified.|
|» record|body|object|false|Field codes and values are specified in this object. If ignored, the record will not be updated. For more information on field types, refer to the following article:<br>[Field Types](https://kintone.dev/en/docs/kintone/overview/field-types/)|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[RecordWritableObject](#schemarecordwritableobject)|false|The value of a single field when writing a record.<br><br>**Always an object with a `value` property, never a bare value.**<br><br>```<br>correct: { "fieldCode": { "value": "ABC" } }<br>wrong:   { "fieldCode": "ABC" }<br>```<br><br>Sending a bare value returns HTTP 400. `type` is optional; when omitted, the App's field settings are used.<br><br>The shape of `value` depends on the field type, which `GET /k/v1/app/form/fields.json` reports:<br><br>\| Field type \| shape of `value` \|<br>\|---\|---\|<br>\| Single-line text, Multi-line text, Rich text, Link, Number, Date, Time, Date and time, Drop-down, Radio button \| string — numbers and dates are strings too, e.g. `"1200000"`, `"2026-08-31"` \|<br>\| Check box, Multi-choice \| array of strings, each matching one of the App's choices exactly \|<br>\| User selection, Department selection, Group selection \| array of `{ "code": "..." }` \|<br>\| Attachment \| array of `{ "fileKey": "..." }` — upload the file first to obtain a key \|<br>\| Table \| array of `{ "id": "...", "value": { "<fieldCode>": { "value": ... } } }` \|<br><br>To clear a field, send an empty string for the text-like types, or an empty array for the array types.<br><br>**A field code that does not exist in the App is silently ignored.** The request still returns HTTP 200 and a new revision, so a typo looks like success even though nothing changed. Copy the codes from `GET /k/v1/app/form/fields.json` exactly.<br><br>**Table and Attachment fields are replaced, not merged.** When updating an existing record, every table row and every `fileKey` the request does not list is deleted. To change one cell of a table, send the whole table including the `id` of each row to keep. Fields left out of the request entirely are untouched.|
|» id|body|integer(int64)|false|The Record ID of the record to be updated. Required, if _updateKey_ will not be specified.|
|» revision|body|integer(int64)|false|The expected revision number. If the value does not match, an error will occur and the record will not be updated. If the value is not specified or is -1, the revision number will not be checked.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "revision": "string"
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

<h3 id="put-record-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of record/put|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

<h3 id="put-record-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|revision|string|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiToken, passwordAuth, oauth2 ( Scopes: k:app_record:write )
</aside>

|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[RecordWritableObject](#schemarecordwritableobject)|false|The value of a single field when writing a record.<br><br>**Always an object with a `value` property, never a bare value.**<br><br>```<br>correct: { "fieldCode": { "value": "ABC" } }<br>wrong:   { "fieldCode": "ABC" }<br>```<br><br>Sending a bare value returns HTTP 400. `type` is optional; when omitted, the App's field settings are used.<br><br>The shape of `value` depends on the field type, which `GET /k/v1/app/form/fields.json` reports:<br><br>\| Field type \| shape of `value` \|<br>\|---\|---\|<br>\| Single-line text, Multi-line text, Rich text, Link, Number, Date, Time, Date and time, Drop-down, Radio button \| string — numbers and dates are strings too, e.g. `"1200000"`, `"2026-08-31"` \|<br>\| Check box, Multi-choice \| array of strings, each matching one of the App's choices exactly \|<br>\| User selection, Department selection, Group selection \| array of `{ "code": "..." }` \|<br>\| Attachment \| array of `{ "fileKey": "..." }` — upload the file first to obtain a key \|<br>\| Table \| array of `{ "id": "...", "value": { "<fieldCode>": { "value": ... } } }` \|<br><br>To clear a field, send an empty string for the text-like types, or an empty array for the array types.<br><br>**A field code that does not exist in the App is silently ignored.** The request still returns HTTP 200 and a new revision, so a typo looks like success even though nothing changed. Copy the codes from `GET /k/v1/app/form/fields.json` exactly.<br><br>**Table and Attachment fields are replaced, not merged.** When updating an existing record, every table row and every `fileKey` the request does not list is deleted. To change one cell of a table, send the whole table including the `id` of each row to keep. Fields left out of the request entirely are untouched.|

## Get records

<a id="opIdgetRecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.cybozu.com/k/v1/records.json?app=0' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cybozu-API-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /k/v1/records.json`

Retrieves details of multiple records from an App by specifying the App ID and a query string.

<h3 id="get-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|app|query|integer(int64)|true|The App ID.|
|query|query|string(query)|false|The search condition, written in Kintone's own query syntax. This is **not** SQL and **not** OData.<br>Ignoring this parameter returns all records that the credential can access.<br><br>The authoritative reference is [Query Strings](https://kintone.dev/en/docs/kintone/overview/query-string/). Its rules are reproduced below so that a correct query can be built without leaving this document.<br><br>## Syntax rules<br><br>- The field code always goes on the **left** of the operator, never on the right.<br>- Wrap string values in double quotes: `Status in ("Closed")`. Numbers and times are unquoted: `price > 10`, `Time > 10:00`.<br>- Combine conditions with `and` / `or`, and group them with parentheses.<br>- Field codes are defined per App and are case-sensitive. Call `GET /k/v1/app/form/fields.json` first to obtain the exact field codes and their types. Do not guess field codes.<br><br>## Operators allowed per field type<br><br>Using an operator that the field type does not support returns an error, so check the field type first.<br><br>\| Field type \| Allowed operators \|<br>\|---\|---\|<br>\| Single-line text, Link \| `=` `!=` `in` `not in` `like` `not like` \|<br>\| Multi-line text \| `like` `not like` `is empty` `is not empty` — **`=` is not allowed** \|<br>\| Rich text \| `like` `not like` \|<br>\| Number, Calculated \| `=` `!=` `>` `<` `>=` `<=` `in` `not in` \|<br>\| Drop-down, Radio button, Check box, Multi-choice \| **`in` / `not in` only — `=` is not allowed** \|<br>\| Date, Date and time, Time \| `=` `!=` `>` `<` `>=` `<=` \|<br>\| Created datetime, Updated datetime \| `=` `!=` `>` `<` `>=` `<=` \|<br>\| User selection, Department selection, Group selection \| `in` `not in` \|<br>\| Created by, Updated by \| `in` `not in` \|<br>\| Status \| `=` `!=` `in` `not in` \|<br>\| Record number, `$id` \| `=` `!=` `>` `<` `>=` `<=` `in` `not in` \|<br>\| Attachment \| `like` `not like` `is empty` `is not empty` \|<br>\| Lookup \| Same as the field type it looks up \|<br>\| Related Records, fields inside a Table \| Same as the source field type, but `=` and `!=` are **not** allowed — use `in` / `not in` \|<br>\| Field group, Category \| Cannot be used in a query \|<br><br>To reference a field inside a Related Records field, use `<relatedRecordsFieldCode>.<fieldCode>`.<br><br>## Functions<br><br>\| Function \| Applies to \|<br>\|---\|---\|<br>\| `LOGINUSER()` \| User selection, Created by, Updated by \|<br>\| `PRIMARY_ORGANIZATION()` \| Department selection \|<br>\| `NOW()` `TODAY()` `YESTERDAY()` `TOMORROW()` \| Date, Date and time, Created datetime, Updated datetime \|<br>\| `FROM_TODAY(n, "DAYS"\\|"WEEKS"\\|"MONTHS"\\|"YEARS")` \| same as above \|<br>\| `THIS_WEEK(SUNDAY..SATURDAY)` `LAST_WEEK()` `NEXT_WEEK()` \| same as above \|<br>\| `THIS_MONTH(1..31\\|LAST)` `LAST_MONTH()` `NEXT_MONTH()` \| same as above \|<br>\| `THIS_YEAR()` `LAST_YEAR()` `NEXT_YEAR()` \| same as above \|<br><br>Arguments may be omitted to mean the whole week / month / year, e.g. `THIS_MONTH()`. Time fields accept no functions.<br><br>## Options<br><br>Place these **after all conditions, in this exact order**: `order by`, `limit`, `offset`.<br><br>\| Option \| Meaning \|<br>\|---\|---\|<br>\| `order by <fieldCode> asc\\|desc` \| Sort order. Separate multiple fields with commas. Defaults to record ID descending. \|<br>\| `limit <n>` \| Number of records to return. Default 100, **maximum 500 for this API**. \|<br>\| `offset <n>` \| Number of records to skip. **Maximum 10000.** To read past 10000 records, use the cursor API (`POST /k/v1/records/cursor.json`) instead. \|<br><br>## Escaping<br><br>Inside double quotes, escape `"` and `\` with a backslash. This is required for single-line text, multi-line text, rich text, check box, radio button, drop-down, multi-choice and status fields.<br>Example: `Checkbox in ("sample\"1\"")`<br><br>## Examples<br><br>```<br>Text like "sample" and Text_area like "sample" order by Created_datetime desc<br>Drop_down in ("value1", "value2") and (Multi_choice in ("value3") or Radio_button in ("value4"))<br>Time > 10:00 and Time < 19:00 and Created_datetime = TODAY() order by $id asc limit 10<br>User_selection in (LOGINUSER()) and Department_selection not in (PRIMARY_ORGANIZATION())<br>Company_DB.company_name in ("kintone") and Company_DB.location like "San Francisco"<br>Text_area is empty<br>```|
|fields|query|[string]|false|The field codes to be included in the response.<br>Ignoring this parameter will return all accessible fields that exist in the App.<br>When specifying this parameter in the request body, the number of field codes that can be specified is up to 1,000.<br>When specifying this parameter in a query string, the maximum index is 99.<br>Fields in a table cannot be specified.<br>To retrieve a field in a table, specify the field code of the table field. All fields in the table will be retrieved.|
|totalCount|query|string(boolean)|false|If set to `true`, the total count of records that match the query conditions will be included in the response.<br>Ignoring this parameter will return `null`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "records": [
    {
      "property1": {
        "type": "CALC",
        "value": "777888999"
      },
      "property2": {
        "type": "CALC",
        "value": "777888999"
      }
    }
  ],
  "totalCount": "string"
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

<h3 id="get-records-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of records/get|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|records|[object]|true|none|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|[RecordObject](#schemarecordobject)|false|none|none|
|totalCount|string \| null|false|none|none|

`POST /k/v1/records.json`

Adds multiple records to an App.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "app": 0,
  "records": [
    {
      "property1": {
        "type": "CHECK_BOX",
        "value": [
          "string"
        ]
      },
      "property2": {

        ]
      }
    }

}
```

<h3 id="post-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» app|body|integer(int64)|true|The App ID.|
|» records|body|[object]|true|Holds an array of record objects, that contains field codes and their values.<br>The values that can be specified vary depending on the type of field.<br>Fields that are not included in the objects are added with their default value.<br>Objects containing field codes that do not exist are ignored.<br>For more information on field types, refer to the following article:<br>[Field Types](https://kintone.dev/en/docs/kintone/overview/field-types/)|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[RecordWritableObject](#schemarecordwritableobject)|false|The value of a single field when writing a record.<br><br>**Always an object with a `value` property, never a bare value.**<br><br>```<br>correct: { "fieldCode": { "value": "ABC" } }<br>wrong:   { "fieldCode": "ABC" }<br>```<br><br>Sending a bare value returns HTTP 400. `type` is optional; when omitted, the App's field settings are used.<br><br>The shape of `value` depends on the field type, which `GET /k/v1/app/form/fields.json` reports:<br><br>\| Field type \| shape of `value` \|<br>\|---\|---\|<br>\| Single-line text, Multi-line text, Rich text, Link, Number, Date, Time, Date and time, Drop-down, Radio button \| string — numbers and dates are strings too, e.g. `"1200000"`, `"2026-08-31"` \|<br>\| Check box, Multi-choice \| array of strings, each matching one of the App's choices exactly \|<br>\| User selection, Department selection, Group selection \| array of `{ "code": "..." }` \|<br>\| Attachment \| array of `{ "fileKey": "..." }` — upload the file first to obtain a key \|<br>\| Table \| array of `{ "id": "...", "value": { "<fieldCode>": { "value": ... } } }` \|<br><br>To clear a field, send an empty string for the text-like types, or an empty array for the array types.<br><br>**A field code that does not exist in the App is silently ignored.** The request still returns HTTP 200 and a new revision, so a typo looks like success even though nothing changed. Copy the codes from `GET /k/v1/app/form/fields.json` exactly.<br><br>**Table and Attachment fields are replaced, not merged.** When updating an existing record, every table row and every `fileKey` the request does not list is deleted. To change one cell of a table, send the whole table including the `id` of each row to keep. Fields left out of the request entirely are untouched.|

```json
  "ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "revisions": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

```json
}
```

## Post records cursor

<a id="opIdpostRecordsCursor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.cybozu.com/k/v1/records/cursor.json \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cybozu-API-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "app": 0,
    "size": 0,
    "query": "string",
    "fields": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /k/v1/records/cursor.json`

Adds a cursor so that large amount of records can be obtained from an App.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "app": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "query": "string",
  "fields": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="post-records-cursor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» app|body|integer(int64)|true|The App ID.|
|» size|body|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of records the Get Cursor API can retrieve from this cursor with one request.<br>The maximum number is 500 records. If ignored, the default number of records to be retrieved is 100.<br>To retrieve all records, repeatedly call the Get Cursor API.<br>For more information, refer to the following article:<br>[Get Cursor](https://kintone.dev/en/docs/kintone/rest-api/records/get-cursor/)|
|» query|body|string(query)|false|The search condition for the records the cursor will walk over, written in Kintone's own query syntax.<br>The operators and functions are the same as for the `query` parameter of `GET /k/v1/records.json` — see that parameter for the table of operators each field type allows.<br><br>**`order by`, `limit` and `offset` cannot be used here.** The cursor manages paging itself: set the batch size with the `size` parameter, then call `GET /k/v1/records/cursor.json` repeatedly until it reports `next: false`.<br><br>Ignoring this parameter creates a cursor over all records that the credential can access.|
|» fields|body|[string]|false|The field codes to be included in the response when using the Get Cursor API. For more information, refer to the following document:<br>[Get Cursor](https://kintone.dev/en/docs/kintone/rest-api/records/get-cursor/)<br>If ignored, all accessible fields in the app will be returned.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "totalCount": "string"
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

<h3 id="post-records-cursor-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of records/cursor/post|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

<h3 id="post-records-cursor-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|none|
|totalCount|string \| null|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiToken, passwordAuth
</aside>

## Put space (guest space)

<a id="opIdputSpaceForGuestSpace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.cybozu.com/k/guest/0/v1/space.json \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cybozu-Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "fixedMember": true,
    "permissions": {
      "createApp": "EVERYONE"
    },
    "name": "string",
    "useMultiThread": true,
    "showMemberList": true,
    "showRelatedLinkList": true,
    "id": 0,
    "isPrivate": true,
    "showAnnouncement": true,
    "showThreadList": true,
    "showAppList": true
  }'
```

`PUT /k/guest/{guestSpaceId}/v1/space.json`

Updates the settings of a Space.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "fixedMember": true,
  "permissions": {
    "createApp": "EVERYONE"
  },
  "name": "string",
  "useMultiThread": true,
  "showMemberList": true,
  "showRelatedLinkList": true,
  "id": 0,
  "isPrivate": true,
  "showAnnouncement": true,
  "showThreadList": true,
  "showAppList": true
}
```

<h3 id="put-space-guest-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|guestSpaceId|path|integer(int64)|true|Guest space ID (the number that appears in the space URL /k/#/space/<ID> when the space is open in a browser).|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» fixedMember|body|boolean|false|The options set for the **Block users from joining or leaving the space and following or unfollowing the threads** setting.<br>`true`: Users cannot join/leave the Space or follow/unfollow threads.<br>`false`: Users can join/leave the Space and follow/unfollow threads.|
|» permissions|body|object|false|An object containing information of the space's permission settings.|
|» » createApp|body|string|false|The option set for the **Only Allow Space Administrators to Create Apps** setting<br>`EVERYONE`: all users can create apps.<br>`ADMIN`: only administrators can create apps.|
|» name|body|string|false|The new name of the Space.|
|» useMultiThread|body|boolean|false|The **Enable multiple threads** setting.<br>`true`: The Space is a Multi-threaded Space.<br>`false`: The setting will not be updated, as a Multi-Threaded Space can not be reverted to a Single-threaded Space.|
|» showMemberList|body|boolean|false|The display status for the **People** widget.<br>`true`: The **People** widget is displayed.<br>`false`: The **People** widget is not displayed.|
|» showRelatedLinkList|body|boolean|false|The display status for the **Related Apps & Spaces** widget.<br>`true`: The **Related Apps & Spaces** widget is displayed.<br>`false`: The **Related Apps & Spaces** widget is not displayed.|
|» id|body|integer(int64)|true|The Space ID.|
|» isPrivate|body|boolean|false|The **Private** settings of the Space.<br>`true`: The Space is private.<br>`false`: The Space is not private.|
|» showAnnouncement|body|boolean|false|The display status for the **Announcement** widget.<br>`true`: The **Announcement** widget is displayed.<br>`false`: The **Announcement** widget is not displayed.|
|» showThreadList|body|boolean|false|The display status for the **Threads** widget.<br>`true`: The **Threads** widget is displayed.<br>`false`: The **Threads** widget is not displayed.|
|» showAppList|body|boolean|false|The display status for the **Apps** widget.<br>`true`: The **Apps** widget is displayed.<br>`false`: The **Apps** widget is not displayed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » createApp|EVERYONE|
|» » createApp|ADMIN|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

<h3 id="put-space-guest-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of space/put|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

```bash
curl https://example.cybozu.com/k/v1/space.json \

    "showThreadList": true,
    "showAppList": true
  }'
```

`PUT /k/v1/space.json`

Updates the settings of a Space.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "fixedMember": true,
  "permissions": {
    "createApp": "EVERYONE"
  },
  "name": "string",
  "useMultiThread": true,
  "showMemberList": true,
  "showRelatedLinkList": true,
  "id": 0,
  "isPrivate": true,
  "showAnnouncement": true,
  "showThreadList": true,
  "showAppList": true
}
```

<h3 id="put-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» fixedMember|body|boolean|false|The options set for the **Block users from joining or leaving the space and following or unfollowing the threads** setting.<br>`true`: Users cannot join/leave the Space or follow/unfollow threads.<br>`false`: Users can join/leave the Space and follow/unfollow threads.|
|» permissions|body|object|false|An object containing information of the space's permission settings.|
|» » createApp|body|string|false|The option set for the **Only Allow Space Administrators to Create Apps** setting<br>`EVERYONE`: all users can create apps.<br>`ADMIN`: only administrators can create apps.|
|» name|body|string|false|The new name of the Space.|
|» useMultiThread|body|boolean|false|The **Enable multiple threads** setting.<br>`true`: The Space is a Multi-threaded Space.<br>`false`: The setting will not be updated, as a Multi-Threaded Space can not be reverted to a Single-threaded Space.|
|» showMemberList|body|boolean|false|The display status for the **People** widget.<br>`true`: The **People** widget is displayed.<br>`false`: The **People** widget is not displayed.|
|» showRelatedLinkList|body|boolean|false|The display status for the **Related Apps & Spaces** widget.<br>`true`: The **Related Apps & Spaces** widget is displayed.<br>`false`: The **Related Apps & Spaces** widget is not displayed.|
|» id|body|integer(int64)|true|The Space ID.|
|» isPrivate|body|boolean|false|The **Private** settings of the Space.<br>`true`: The Space is private.<br>`false`: The Space is not private.|
|» showAnnouncement|body|boolean|false|The display status for the **Announcement** widget.<br>`true`: The **Announcement** widget is displayed.<br>`false`: The **Announcement** widget is not displayed.|
|» showThreadList|body|boolean|false|The display status for the **Threads** widget.<br>`true`: The **Threads** widget is displayed.<br>`false`: The **Threads** widget is not displayed.|
|» showAppList|body|boolean|false|The display status for the **Apps** widget.<br>`true`: The **Apps** widget is displayed.<br>`false`: The **Apps** widget is not displayed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » createApp|EVERYONE|
|» » createApp|ADMIN|

```json
{}
```

```json
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
```

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.cybozu.com/k/v1/space/body.json \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cybozu-Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "id": 0,
    "body": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /k/v1/space/body.json`

Updates the body of a Space.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "body": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="put-space-body-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» id|body|integer(int64)|true|The Space ID.|
|» body|body|string|true|The contents of the body as an HTML string.<br>HTML tags that cannot be used will be automatically removed.<br>HTML can be used to attach Apps, files and Emoji.<br>The usage of the @ mark to mention a user will not notify that user.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

<h3 id="put-space-body-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of space/body/put|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
passwordAuth
</aside>

## Put space thread

<a id="opIdputSpaceThread"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.cybozu.com/k/v1/space/thread.json \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  }'
```

`PUT /k/v1/space/thread.json`

Updates a Thread of a Space.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "id": 0,
  "body": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="put-space-thread-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The new name of the Thread.<br>Must be between 1 - 128 characters.<br>The name will not be updated if this parameter is ignored.<br>The Thread name of single threaded Spaces cannot be updated.|
|» id|body|integer(int64)|true|The Thread ID.<br>The Thread ID can be found in the URL of the Thread.<br>A Space with the URL of `https://{subdomain}.kintone.com/k/#/space/111/thread/222` has a Space ID of 111 and a Thread ID of 222.|
|» body|body|string|false|The contents of the Thread body.<br>Write the contents as an HTML string, within 65535 characters.<br>If the [Frontend Framework Revamp](https://kintone.dev/en/id/bbfaa03dedc276890f5db503/#frontend-revamp) is enabled on the Space and Thread pages, the maximum limit is 100,000 characters.<br>The Thread body will not be updated if this parameter is ignored.<br>HTML tags that cannot be used will be automatically removed.<br>HTML can be used to attach Apps, files and Emoji.<br>The usage of the @ mark to mention a user will not notify that user.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

<h3 id="put-space-thread-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of space/thread/put|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
passwordAuth
</aside>

`POST /k/v1/space/thread/comment.json`

Adds a comment to a Thread of a Space.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": {
    "mentions": [
      {
        "code": "string",
        "type": "USER"
      }
    ],
    "files": [

        "fileKey": "string"
      }
    ],
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|» » mentions|body|[[SpaceThreadCommentPostMentionForm](#schemaspacethreadcommentpostmentionform)]|false|An array including mentions, that notify other Kintone users.|
|» » files|body|[[SpaceThreadCommentPostFileForm](#schemaspacethreadcommentpostfileform)]|false|An array including data of attachment files.<br>The maximum number of the files is 5.<br>Required, if comment.text is not set.|
|» » text|body|string|false|The comment contents.<br>A line break can be specified by LF.<br>The maximum characters of the comment is 65535.<br>If the [Frontend Framework Revamp](https://kintone.dev/en/id/bbfaa03dedc276890f5db503/#frontend-revamp) is enabled on the Space and Thread pages, the maximum limit is 100,000 characters.<br>Required, if comment.files is not set.|

```json
}
```

<h1 id="kintone-rest-api-templates">TEMPLATES</h1>

## Post template space (guest space)

<a id="opIdpostTemplateSpaceForGuestSpace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.cybozu.com/k/guest/0/v1/template/space.json \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cybozu-Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "fixedMember": true,
    "isGuest": true,
    "members": [
      {
        "isAdmin": true,
        "includeSubs": true,
        "entity": {
          "code": "string",
          "type": "USER"
        }
      }
    ],
    "name": "string",
    "id": 0,
    "isPrivate": true
  }'
```

`POST /k/guest/{guestSpaceId}/v1/template/space.json`

Creates a Space from a Space template.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "fixedMember": true,
  "isGuest": true,
  "members": [
    {
      "isAdmin": true,
      "includeSubs": true,
      "entity": {
        "code": "string",
        "type": "USER"
      }
    }
  ],
  "name": "string",
  "id": 0,
  "isPrivate": true
}
```

<h3 id="post-template-space-guest-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|guestSpaceId|path|integer(int64)|true|Guest space ID (the number that appears in the space URL /k/#/space/<ID> when the space is open in a browser).|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» fixedMember|body|boolean|false|The "**Block users from joining or leaving the space and following or unfollowing the threads.**" settings of the Space.<br>- `true`: Users will not be able to join/leave the Space or follow/unfollow threads.<br>- `false`: Users will be able to join/leave the Space and follow/unfollow threads.<br>If ignored, this value is `false`.|
|» isGuest|body|boolean|false|The Guest Space settings of the Space.<br>- `true`: The Space will be a Guest Space<br>- `false`: The Space will be a normal Space.<br>If ignored, this value is `false`.|
|» members|body|[[TemplateSpacePostMemberForm](#schematemplatespacepostmemberform)]|false|A list of members of the Space.<br>At least one Space Administrator must be specified.<br>Inactive and deleted users cannot be specified.|
|» name|body|string|true|The new name of the Space.|
|» id|body|integer(int64)|true|The Space Template ID.<br>For instructions on creating Space Templates, refer to the following article:<br>[Creating a Template from a Space](https://us.kintone.help/k/en/id/04075)<br>The Space Template ID is listed on the Space Templates list page, found under https://{domainname}.kintone.com/k/admin/system/spacetemplate/|
|» isPrivate|body|boolean|false|The "**Private**" settings of the Space.<br>- `true`: The Space will be Private.<br>- `false`: The Space will not be Private.<br>If the **isGuest** parameter is set to `true`, this value is also `true`.<br>If ignored, this value is `false`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string"
}
```

> 4XX Response

```json
{
  "id": "1505999166-897850006",
  "code": "CB_IJ01",
  "message": "Invalid JSON string."
}
```

<h3 id="post-template-space-guest-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|success case of template/space/post|Inline|
|4XX|Client Error|Error response. When a request fails, an HTTP status code other than 2xx is returned together with an error object containing id / code / message.|[KintoneError](#schemakintoneerror)|

<h3 id="post-template-space-guest-space-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
passwordAuth
</aside>

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|
|recordImportable|boolean|false|none|The file import permission of the entity.<br>The record add permissions must also be enabled to set this value as `true`.<br>- `true`: Files will be importable<br>- `false`: Files will not be importable<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|appEditable|boolean|false|none|The App management permission of the entity.<br>- The App's settings will be accessible.<br>- The App's settings will not be accessible.<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|recordExportable|boolean|false|none|The file export permission of the entity.<br>- `true`: Files will be exportable<br>- `false`: Files will not be exportable<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|recordAddable|boolean|false|none|The record add permission of the entity<br>- `true`: Records can be added.<br>- `false`: Records cannot be added.<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|recordViewable|boolean|false|none|The record view permission of the entity.<br>- `true`: Records will be viewable.<br>- `false`: Records will not be viewable.<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|recordEditable|boolean|false|none|The record edit permission of the entity.<br>The record view permissions must also be enabled to set this value as `true`.<br>- `true`: Records will be editable.<br>- `false`: Records will not be editable.<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|recordDeletable|boolean|false|none|The record delete permission of the entity.<br>The record view permissions must also be enabled to set this value as `true`.<br>- `true`: Records will be deletable.<br>- `false`: Records will not be deletable.<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|includeSubs|boolean|false|none|The permission inheritance settings of the department the permission is granted to. This parameter is available if "ORGANIZATION" is specified for the **rights[].entity.type** parameter.<br>- `true`: Permissions will be inherited.<br>- `false`: Permissions will not be inherited.<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|entity|object|true|none|An object containing data of the entity the permission is granted to.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|recordImportable|boolean|false|none|The file import permission of the entity.<br>The record add permissions must also be enabled to set this value as `true`.<br>- `true`: Files will be importable<br>- `false`: Files will not be importable<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|appEditable|boolean|false|none|The App management permission of the entity.<br>- The App's settings will be accessible.<br>- The App's settings will not be accessible.<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|recordExportable|boolean|false|none|The file export permission of the entity.<br>- `true`: Files will be exportable<br>- `false`: Files will not be exportable<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|recordAddable|boolean|false|none|The record add permission of the entity<br>- `true`: Records can be added.<br>- `false`: Records cannot be added.<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|recordViewable|boolean|false|none|The record view permission of the entity.<br>- `true`: Records will be viewable.<br>- `false`: Records will not be viewable.<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|recordEditable|boolean|false|none|The record edit permission of the entity.<br>The record view permissions must also be enabled to set this value as `true`.<br>- `true`: Records will be editable.<br>- `false`: Records will not be editable.<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|recordDeletable|boolean|false|none|The record delete permission of the entity.<br>The record view permissions must also be enabled to set this value as `true`.<br>- `true`: Records will be deletable.<br>- `false`: Records will not be deletable.<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|includeSubs|boolean|false|none|The permission inheritance settings of the department the permission is granted to. This parameter is available if "ORGANIZATION" is specified for the **rights[].entity.type** parameter.<br>- `true`: Permissions will be inherited.<br>- `false`: Permissions will not be inherited.<br>If ignored, this value is false.|
|entity|object|true|none|An object containing data of the entity the permission is granted to.|
